name: Peltast Troop
body:
Peltast Troop
CR 8

Wielding javelins and various light weapons, these nimble fighters weave and dart through any cover they can find across the battlefield while harrying their foes.

XP 4,800
N Medium humanoid (human, troop)
Init +8; Senses Perception +18

DEFENSE

AC 22, touch 15, flat-footed 17 (+7 armor, +4 Dex, +1 dodge)
hp 104 (11d8+50)
Fort +7, Ref +11, Will +7
Defensive Abilities troop traits

OFFENSE

Speed 40 ft.
Melee troop (2d6+5)
Space 20 ft.; Reach 5 ft.
Special Attacks skirmishers

STATISTICS

Str 20, Dex 19, Con 19, Int 10, Wis 14, Cha 13
Base Atk +8; CMB +13; CMD 27
Feats Dodge, Improved Initiative, Iron Will, Mobility, Skill Focus (Perception), Toughness
Skills Knowledge (local, nature) +8, Perception +18, Stealth +6
Languages Common
SQ favored enemy, skirmishers

SPECIAL ABILITIES

Favored Enemy (Ex)

Peltasts spend their training studying the techniques of a specific enemy, often a foreign country and its armies rather than a creature type or subtype, and specifically learning how to defeat its troops in their homeland. This training and hatred grant the peltast troop a +2 bonus on Perception checks, troop melee damage, and damage rolls when facing other troop units. Their training also grants the peltasts a +3 bonus on all Knowledge (local) and Knowledge (nature) checks. The bonuses on Knowledge checks are calculated into the troop’s stat block.

Skirmish (Ex)

Peltasts are effective and versatile hit-and-run troops.

This lowers the troop’s AC by 2 and its troop melee damage by one die but increases its movement by 10 feet (these effects have already been calculated into the troop’s stat block). Additionally, as a standard action, the troop can make a ranged attack similar to a volley. This attack can take the form of up to two lines starting from the corner of any square in the troop’s space. This attack’s range is 50 feet. All creatures in these lines take 3d6+5 points of piercing damage (Reflex DC 19 half). The save DC is Dexterity-based.

ECOLOGY

Environment any temperate land
Organization solitary, pair, or army (3-6 troops)
Treasure standard

Peltast troops often form along borders in response to foreign aggression, bringing irregular troops that emphasize mobility in to guard the flanks of heavier infantry and screening and scouting along the lines of march. These troops may be highly trained and regulated, but many form almost organically around like-minded local leaders and may gather, fight, and disperse after meeting a specific goal—or after an opposing army scatters them to the winds. troop, phalanx Marching forward with expressionless faces, these soldiers carry stout spears and heavy shields shields with the symbol of their nation stamped on them.
